subject.title: fix(compaction): prevent repeated restarts after safety timeouts

question: Should native compaction results produced immediately after wrapper-owned safety-timeout cancellation be allowed to persist while that exact timeout's bounded acceptance window remains open?
rationale: Code and proof support the narrow mechanics, but changing timeout cancellation from always fail-closed to conditionally committing session state is a product reliability policy choice that automation cannot authorize.

options.title: Accept bounded partial commits
options.body: Allow only marked, entry-aligned partial results tied to the exact wrapper timeout and land after current-head checks remain green.

options.title: Keep native timeout fail-closed
options.body: Retain inner chunk partial-summary recovery and timeout guidance but remove the post-timeout AgentSession commit exception.

options.title: Require live slow-provider proof
options.body: Pause until a realistic gateway run demonstrates timeout recovery and lifecycle cleanup under a slow provider or delayed compaction hook.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded partial commits
recommendation.body: Allow only marked, entry-aligned partial results tied to the exact wrapper timeout and land after current-head checks remain green.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the assigned reviewer and the strongest recent history match for the compaction timeout ownership boundary.
